sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry in two independent cell lines (HEK 293 and BWZ.36); no functional assay of native CRTAM activity was reported for this chimeric construct.
sites.rationale: The paper describes an N-terminal FLAG tag on the CRTAM extracellular Ig domains in a membrane-anchored chimeric construct; no residue number is stated, but 'N-terminal' combined with the signal-peptide topology (SP cleavage after residue 17, mature N-terminus at residue 18) leaves exactly one extracellular terminus, placing the junction unambiguously at insert_after_residue=17. Python confirmed residue 17 = A and residue 18 = S from the canonical sequence. The tag is 272 residues from the TM boundary and well within the extracellular domain. The construct is membrane-anchored (not a soluble ectodomain) and surface display was validated by flow cytometry, satisfying the ledger qualification criteria. A chimeric construct was engineered in which an N-terminal FLAG epitope tag was placed upstream of both CRTAM extracellular Ig domains (residues 18–289), fused to the chicken CD8α transmembrane domain and murine CD3ζ cytoplasmic domain; the construct was stably expressed in HEK 293 and BWZ.36 cells.

sources.claim: In order to produce a CRTAM specific mab we generated two cell lines with a N-terminal FLAG-tagged CRTAM version that displayed both extracellular Ig domains fused to the chicken CD8 transmembrane and murine CD3ζ cytoplasmic domains.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) from PMC3858274 describe the same construct and the same N-terminal FLAG site; L1 is cited as the primary clip because it most completely describes the construct design. L2 and L3 provide independent flow-cytometry confirmation of surface display. L4 provides cloning details confirming the N-terminal FLAG position in the vector. The chimeric nature of the construct (heterologous TM/cyto domains) does not disqualify it because the CRTAM extracellular Ig domains are intact and the construct is membrane-anchored and surface-displayed. No residue number is stated in any ledger line, so position_evidence is topology_derived rather than validated. No other sites are supported by the ledger: there are no reports of internal loop insertions, C-terminal extracellular tags, or intracellular tags for CRTAM in the provided evidence.
